name: Ternary Bonsai 2 27B
tagline: PrismML's ternary trick, round two: 98.2% of Qwen3.8-27B in a 5.9 GB file — Apache, with the license in the repo
description: Two months after the first Bonsai release, PrismML's second-generation ternary compression of Qwen3.8-27B lands at 9x smaller than its full-precision base while retaining a claimed 98.2% of aggregate benchmark performance. The distribution hub is the -gguf repo: a 5.95 GB PTQ1_0 file and a 7.21 GB PQ2_0 alongside the 53.8 GB F16 reference, a later 7.63 GB Q2_0 build, and mmproj files that keep the base model's vision path intact, with MLX 2-bit builds in the same collection. PrismML says the biggest change from gen one is simply quality — same footprint, better model.
why: Gen-one Bonsai 27B is already on our shelf as the proof that 2-bit ternary quantization had graduated from paper to product; gen two is the cadence proof. And the paperwork improved along with the weights: where the first release leaned on card tags, the Bonsai 2 gguf repo carries an actual LICENSE file — the standard Apache-2.0 text (10,174 bytes, appendix unfilled), re-read on 2026-11-01, with a NOTICE.txt beside it. Base-model lineage is clean too: Qwen3.8-27B is Apache-2.0 with a LICENSE file, per our existing entry. Apache in, Apache out, and file-verified at both ends — plus PrismML's runtime code (a llama.cpp fork and a demo repo) is open under MIT and Apache-2.0 respectively.
useCases: Frontier-adjacent local inference on 8–16 GB machines — a 27B-class multimodal model in under 6 GB
Offline and air-gapped deployments where every gigabyte of the artifact matters
Comparing ternary quantization against GGUF Q-quants of the same base — the F16 reference ships in the same repo
audience: Local-AI users on modest hardware, edge deployers, and quantization researchers

setup.requirements: llama.cpp-compatible runtimes for the GGUF builds — the PTQ/PQ formats are supported by PrismML's llama.cpp fork, so check which file your build can load; MLX 2-bit builds for Apple Silicon; the F16 reference wants ~54 GB of headroom

license.notes: Re-verified 2026-11-01. Weights: the prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf HF repo is tagged apache-2.0 and holds a standalone 10,174-byte LICENSE (read directly: standard Apache-2.0 template headed 'Apache License', appendix unfilled — the size difference from the canonical 11.4 kB) and a 411-byte NOTICE.txt, unchanged in size since 2026-09-21; no riders, territory clauses, or use restrictions found. Base: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B is Apache-2.0 with its own LICENSE file per our catalog entry, so the derivative chain is Apache end to end. Code: PrismML's companion repos are open — PrismML-Eng/Bonsai-demo reports Apache-2.0 and PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp (a fork) reports MIT on GitHub; the weights repo itself contains no code. A step up from gen one, which we verified via runtime forks and card tags; this generation puts the license text in the weights repo itself.

tally.stars: 2.9k HF likes and ~1.85M downloads last month on the -gguf repo; the companion GitHub repos show 3.5k stars (Bonsai-demo) and 990 stars (llama.cpp fork)
tally.lastActivity: Announced September 17, 2026; HF repo last updated October 30 (Q2_0 file documented); companion repos pushed in late October

limitations: The 98.2% retention figure is PrismML's own aggregate and deserves task-level scrutiny — ternary models historically degrade unevenly, with long-tail knowledge and edge-case reasoning suffering first; PQ/PTQ formats need runtime support (PrismML maintains a fork for exactly this), and a separate -gguf-dev repo exists for builds that need the fork, so confirm which file matches your runtime before assuming it just loads.
take: The first Bonsai asked whether ternary compression was real. The second one answers a better question: can it keep up with the release cadence of the models it compresses? Two months base-to-derivative, with the license file where it belongs. That's a supply chain, not a stunt.
